person.organisation: Studio Nordlicht, a three-person brand and web studio
person.summary: Runs client website projects from design to launch with a designer and a freelance developer. Uses ChatGPT and Claude for writing, Claude Code and Codex for site builds and small scripts. Weekly rhythm: planning on Monday, client calls midweek, status mails and content on Friday.

headline: Client updates, proposals and invoicing come back every week. Agents can draft them and give you 3 to 4 hours back.

findings.title: Weekly client status mails
findings.detail: Every Friday afternoon two or three client updates are written from rough notes in ChatGPT, then shortened in a second turn.

evidence.observation: 28 status mails over 14 Fridays, written from rough notes and then shortened in a second request every time.
Weekly one-hour block on Friday for client status mails

findings.title: Proposals from discovery-call notes
findings.detail: Call notes become a proposal with the same five parts every time; day rate and a translation for a co-founder are added in follow-ups.

evidence.observation: You wrote 11 proposals in three months, each with the same five parts and the same two follow-ups: the day rate, then an English scope.
4 more proposal drafts and a project called Proposals with the structure as instructions
A proposal template with goals, scope, timeline, price and next steps

findings.title: Monthly invoicing from time tracking
findings.detail: On the first working day the time-tracking export is grouped per client project into invoice lines for the invoicing tool, by a script and with Claude Code.

evidence.observation: Three Claude Code sessions on the 1st or 2nd of the month turned the time export into invoice lines, and the invoice script only runs then.
The invoice script runs only in the first three days of a month
Two-hour block for invoicing and reminders on the first Monday of each month

findings.title: Chasing unpaid invoices
findings.detail: Reminders for overdue invoices are written by hand, and the person's memory notes say chasing invoices is disliked.

evidence.observation: 3 reminder mails for invoices 14 days overdue, plus a stated dislike of chasing invoices in memory

findings.title: Call notes to tasks for the team
findings.detail: After client calls, notes are turned into tasks with owners and due dates for the designer, the developer and the founder in Notion.

evidence.observation: Ten times you turned call notes into Notion tasks by hand, after about two and a half client calls a week.
About 2.5 external calls a week (discovery and review calls)

findings.title: LinkedIn posts about launches
findings.detail: Monday posts about a recent launch, always with a request for alternative hooks; a Friday content block exists.

evidence.observation: Nine LinkedIn drafts, all on Mondays, each followed by a request for two more hooks.
4 portfolio case studies written from project notes

findings.title: Brand voice re-explained in every chat
findings.detail: Website copy is rewritten in the studio's voice, and the voice rules are pasted into the prompt each time although a guide exists.

evidence.observation: 9 copy rewrites that restate the voice rules, plus a separate brand-voice project
A brand voice guide in the studio folder

findings.title: Website launch QA
findings.detail: Before each launch the same checklist runs in Claude Code: speed scores, alt texts in German, links, meta data, then a short summary for the client.

evidence.observation: Three launches, the same checklist and the same three requests each time.
A saved launch checklist of eight points

findings.title: Weekly site health check
findings.detail: A script checks all client sites for broken links every Monday; it was recently extended to SSL expiry and page speed.

evidence.observation: The link-check script ran sixteen Mondays in a row.
2 sessions building and extending the checker, with the wish to run it every Monday

findings.title: Replies to website inquiries
findings.detail: Contact-form inquiries get a reply offering two call slots and a booking link.

evidence.observation: Ten replies to website inquiries, each offering two call slots and the booking link.

findings.title: Monday planning
findings.detail: A weekly planning hour on Monday morning; client work and scripts start right after it.

evidence.observation: A one-hour planning block every Monday at 9:00.

findings.title: Six hours of meetings a week
findings.detail: Stand-ups, a weekly client check-in, discovery and review calls add up to about six hours a week; preparation and follow-up add to it.

evidence.observation: About 6.4 meeting hours a week, 2.5 of the calls with external guests

findings.title: Small team, clear roles
findings.detail: The founder writes, sells and invoices; a designer works in Figma; a freelance developer builds in Webflow and code.

evidence.observation: Memory describes a three-person studio and who does what

findings.title: Processes already written down
findings.detail: Templates and checklists exist for proposals, status mails, launches, client onboarding and invoicing, a ready base for Knowledge.

evidence.observation: 2 templates, 3 process documents and a brand guide in the studio folder

workflows.title: Friday client updates
steps_today: Collect the week's notes per client
Paste them into ChatGPT with the tone rules
Ask for a shorter version
Copy into a mail and send

steps: Every Friday at 14:00 the Clients manager reads the week's Notion tasks, call notes and Slack threads per active project
It posts one draft per client in the Clients Space chat, in German and in the studio's voice
You edit a line if needed and send it yourself, nothing is sent without you
Save the status template and the voice rules as a ChatGPT project or Claude project
Keep one running note per client during the week
On Friday paste each note into the project and review the draft
own_tools.prompt: Write this week's status update for the client below, in German, friendly and short (max 120 words). Structure: done, next, what we need from you. Sign as the studio. Notes: <paste notes>

saving.note: Minutes from the weekly Friday calendar block.

agent_card.name: Status writer
agent_card.role: Drafts the weekly client status update from the week's notes and tasks.
agent_card.instructions: Every Friday, for each active client project, read this week's tasks, call notes and team chat threads. Write one status update per client in German, friendly and at most 120 words, in three parts: done, next, what we need from you. Follow the brand voice and the status template. Add the staging link when there is one. Deliver the drafts for review; never send them.
agent_card.approval: A person reads and sends each mail.

fit.if_wrong: A draft with a wrong date; you read every one before sending.
fit.note: Drafts are ready before your Friday slot; you only read and send.

workflows.title: Proposals from call notes
steps_today: Paste call notes into ChatGPT or Claude
Ask for the usual five-part structure
Add the day rate and split design and build
Translate the scope when needed
Move it into the template

steps: Paste the call notes in the New business Space and mention the Proposal writer
It follows the proposal skill: goals, scope, timeline, price from the price list, next steps, plus an English scope when asked
You get a Word document to review; the maintenance retainer is always offered
Create a Claude project or custom GPT named Proposals with the template and price list as files
After each call paste the notes with one prompt
Export to the document template
own_tools.prompt: Turn these discovery call notes into a proposal with: goals, scope, timeline, price (day rate from the price list, split design and build), next steps, and a maintenance retainer option. German. Notes: <paste notes>

saving.note: 11 proposals in about three months; two hours each is a typical value.

agent_card.name: Proposal writer
agent_card.role: Turns discovery-call notes into a proposal in the studio's structure.
agent_card.instructions: Turn the call notes into a proposal with five parts: goals, scope, timeline, price, next steps. Price from the price list: day rate, split into design and build, and always offer a maintenance retainer. German unless asked; add an English scope section when asked. If budget, deadline or page count is missing, ask one question first. Deliver a document for review.
agent_card.approval: A person reviews and sends the proposal.

fit.who_waits: The client waits for the proposal, now a day less.
fit.if_wrong: A wrong price; the price list is the only source and you review.
fit.note: The draft is there minutes after the call instead of the next evening.

workflows.title: Monthly invoicing and reminders
workflows.trigger: First working day of the month
steps_today: Export last month's hours from time tracking
Run the invoice script or ask Claude Code to group them
Paste the lines into the invoicing tool
Find overdue invoices and write reminders

steps: On the first working day the Finance manager reads last month's hours from Toggl Track
It posts invoice lines per client project at the day rate, flags hours without a project, and lists invoices unpaid after 14 days
It drafts reminder mails in the billing inbox; you check and send them
Keep the invoice script and put a monthly reminder in the calendar for the first working day
Turn on automatic payment reminders in the invoicing tool
Use a saved prompt for the rare personal reminder

saving.note: Two-hour calendar block plus about 30 minutes of reminders a month.

agent_card.name: Invoice preparer
agent_card.role: Prepares monthly invoice lines and overdue reminders.

trigger.when: First working day of the month, 9:00

agent_card.instructions: Read last month's tracked hours and group them per client project. Make one invoice line per project at the day rate from the price list and flag entries without a project. Then list invoices unpaid for more than 14 days and draft a polite German reminder for each. Deliver the lines as a table and the reminders as drafts. Never book invoices, send mails or move money.
agent_card.approval: A person books the invoices and sends the reminders.

fit.who_waits: Nobody; invoices go out on the same day as before.
fit.if_wrong: A missed project; entries without a project are flagged.
fit.note: Same day as today, without the two hours of copying.

workflows.title: Call notes to team tasks
steps_today: Write notes during the call
Ask ChatGPT for action items with owners and dates
Create the tasks in Notion by hand

steps: Drop the call notes into the client's project chat in the Clients Space
The Clients manager creates the Notion tasks with owner and due date and posts the list
A check also picks up new notes added in Notion every 30 minutes
Use a Notion template for call notes with an action-items table
Ask Notion AI or ChatGPT to fill owners and dates
Turn on Notion's database reminders for due dates

saving.note: Counts all client calls (about 2.5 a week), not only the 10 explicit requests.

agent_card.name: Call-notes tasker
agent_card.role: Turns client call notes into tasks with owners and due dates.
agent_card.instructions: For each new call note, list the action items. Give each an owner (founder, designer or developer) and a due date; use the next call date when none is said. Create the tasks on the task board and post the list back to the project.

fit.who_waits: The designer and developer get tasks right after the call.
fit.if_wrong: A wrong owner; the list is posted for everyone to see.
fit.note: Tasks appear while the call is still fresh.

workflows.title: LinkedIn post about a launch
steps_today: Pick a recent launch
Ask ChatGPT for a post
Ask for alternative hooks
Post by hand

steps: Every Friday at 15:30 the New business manager reads the last two weeks of launches and case studies
It posts two drafts with three hooks each in the Space chat, in the studio's voice
You pick one and post it yourself
Keep an idea list per launch
Save one prompt with the voice rules
Block the Friday content slot you already have
own_tools.prompt: Draft a LinkedIn post (max 120 words) about this launch: the client's problem, what we built, one result. Then give three alternative opening hooks. No hashtag lists. Facts: <paste>

saving.note: Minutes from the Friday content block.

agent_card.name: Post drafter
agent_card.role: Drafts LinkedIn posts about recent launches.
agent_card.instructions: Look at launches and case studies from the past two weeks. Draft two LinkedIn posts of at most 120 words: the client's problem, what was built, one result. Give three alternative opening hooks for each. Use the brand voice; no hashtag lists. Deliver the drafts; never post.
agent_card.approval: A person picks one and posts it.

fit.if_wrong: A weak hook; you pick and post yourself.
fit.note: Same Friday slot, with drafts ready.

workflows.title: Website launch QA
steps_today: Run the launch checklist in Claude Code
Fix alt texts and meta data
Write a QA summary for the client

steps: Ask the Launch QA agent in the client's project chat to run the launch check
It works through the launch skill in the agent's browser on your Mac: speed, alt texts, links, meta, 404, redirects
It posts the fixes needed and a short client summary as a draft
Keep the checklist as a template
Run PageSpeed Insights and a free link checker
Use a saved prompt for the client summary

saving.note: About one launch a month; 90 minutes is a typical value.

agent_card.name: Launch checker
agent_card.role: Runs the launch checklist on a client site before it goes live.
agent_card.instructions: Open the site and check: speed scores above 90 on mobile and desktop, alt texts present and in German, no broken links, meta titles and descriptions, favicon, 404 page, redirects from old URLs, cookie banner, Search Console access. List the fixes, most important first, with the page for each. Then draft a five-line summary for the client.
agent_card.approval: A person fixes issues and sends the summary.

fit.if_wrong: A missed check; the checklist is the same every time.
fit.note: The checklist runs in minutes instead of a session.

workflows.title: Weekly site health check
steps_today: Run the link checker in the terminal
Read the output
Fix or forward problems

steps: Every Monday at 7:00 Launch QA checks all client sites for broken links, SSL expiry and speed
It stays quiet when all is fine and posts in the Clients Space only when something needs attention
Schedule the existing script with cron or a Shortcuts automation every Monday
Add a free uptime monitor with SSL alerts

agent_card.name: Site monitor
agent_card.role: Checks all live client sites every week.
agent_card.instructions: Check every live client site for broken links, SSL certificates expiring within 30 days, and mobile speed below 80. Report only problems, one line each with the site and what to fix. If all is fine, stay silent.

fit.if_wrong: A false alarm; it posts only problems.
fit.note: Problems surface on Monday morning without running the script.

workflows.title: Reply to website inquiries
steps_today: Read the inquiry
Ask ChatGPT for a reply with two slots
Add the booking link and send

steps: A check looks at the contact inbox every 15 minutes
For a new project request the New business manager drafts a reply with the booking link and posts a one-line summary in the Space chat
You send the draft after a glance
Save a reply template with the booking link
Add a mail filter that labels contact-form mails
Put the booking link in the form's confirmation message

agent_card.name: Inquiry responder
agent_card.role: Drafts replies to new project inquiries.

trigger.when: A new mail arrives in the contact inbox

agent_card.instructions: If the mail is a new project inquiry, draft a reply: thank them, repeat what they asked for in one line, two lines on how the studio works, and the booking link for a 30-minute call. German unless they wrote in English. Post a one-line summary with what they want and any budget. Skip newsletters and notifications.

fit.who_waits: The person who wrote in waits less.
fit.if_wrong: A reply to a newsletter; drafts are never sent without you.
fit.note: A draft is ready within 15 minutes of the mail.

workflows.title: Monday plan for the week
steps_today: Look through the calendar and open tasks
Decide the week's priorities

steps: At 8:30 on Monday your assistant reads the week's calendar and your mail
It sends you a short brief: calls to prepare, deadlines, three suggested priorities
Keep a weekly planning note template
Ask your AI tool each Monday with your calendar pasted in

saving.note: Only the preparation part of the planning hour.

agent_card.name: Week planner
agent_card.role: Prepares a short brief for Monday planning.
agent_card.instructions: Read this week's calendar and last week's unanswered mail. Write a brief under 200 words: calls that need preparation with one line of context each, deadlines, threads waiting on a reply, and three suggested priorities.

fit.if_wrong: A missed call in the brief; the calendar stays the source.
fit.note: Ready when the planning hour starts.

quick_wins.title: Write the brand voice down once
quick_wins.how: Nine chats restated the same voice rules. Save the guide in Company knowledge and no prompt needs them again.

quick_wins.title: Turn on the Friday drafts
quick_wins.how: The drafts are waiting at 14:00. You read, change a line, send.

quick_wins.title: Give the next proposal to an agent
quick_wins.how: Paste the notes from your next discovery call and compare the draft with your own.

watch_outs: Client mails and invoice reminders stay drafts; Send is set to Ask each time everywhere.
Invoices involve money: the Finance Space is Members only and the agent prepares lines, it never books or sends invoices.
Lexoffice is not in the app list yet; invoice lines arrive as a table to paste, as today.
The contact inbox check assumes a shared studio inbox; with only a personal inbox, the assistant handles inquiries instead.
not_used: A tax question and a recipe

working_model.summary: Works office hours in a steady weekly rhythm: planning on Monday, calls midweek, writing on Friday.

facts.text: Most writing happens on Fridays and Mondays.

hypotheses.text: Client mails can wait until Friday afternoon; nobody needs them earlier.
Anything that goes to a client needs your eyes before it is sent.
Invoices can be prepared by an agent, but you book them yourself.
hypotheses.answer: Yes, and reminders too: you send those yourself.

off_limits: Sending anything to clients without review

dropped.title: Automatic sending of status mails
dropped.why: Client mails stay with you; drafts save the time without the risk.
